text: Participants will watch videos of car crashes in slow motion. They will then evaluate how hard each crash seemed, and guess how many people were hurt in each crash.
Participants will play a video game in which they murder crowds of people with a machine gun. Their aggression levels will be measured.
Participants will take a math test with four other people, who will encourage them to cheat on the test. Their cheating behavior will be observed.
Participants will listen to audio tapes of crying babies using headphones. Their heart rate and stress levels will be measured.
Participants who dislike cats will be put in a room with three cats and asked to befriend them. After, the participants will fill a questionnaire about liking cats.
Participants will be asked to write an essay about how they would feel if their significant other broke up with them.
Participants will be asked to count how many jellybeans are in a jar while random numbers are being played to them through headphones. Their math accuracy will be measured.
Participants will be presented with an unsolvable technology problem involving a printer. They will then be asked to rate their frustration.
Participants will be asked to enter an elevator full of people, and face away from the door for the entire ride. They will then be asked how awkward they felt.
Participants will view a series of colored dots and determine the color of each dot. Their ability to tell colors apart will be measured.
Participants will be asked to burn an American flag using a lighter. Their political attitudes and national pride will be measured.
Participants will peel potatoes. Afterwards, they will give their opinions about a list of food products that all contain potatoes.
Participants will be asked to sort a bag of glitter by color with their hands. The time it takes them to sort the bag will be measured.
Participants will take part in a practice job interview. At the end of the interview they will rate their conversation partner on different personality measures.
Participants will be asked to rank books from best to worst based only on their covers. Their preferences will be measured.
Participants will play a card game while loud music plays in the background. Their frustration levels will be recorded.
Participants will take a math test during which it is easy to cheat by looking at another person's exam. Their decision whether or not to cheat will be observed.
Participants will be insulted and then asked to bend a spoon with their bare hands. The amount they bend the spoon will be measured.
Participants will be asked to deliver increasingly high-voltage electric shocks to a person in another room. The shocks are not real. Distress levels will be recorded.
Participants who are depressed will read information about the efficacy of a new antidepressant medication. They will then indicate whether they intend to try the new medication.
Participants will drink as much water as they possible can in a short period of time, and then to run on a treadmill. Afterwards, they will be asked to rate how sick they feel.
Participants will watch videos of an awkward social interaction, and then write suggestions on how they would make the interaction less awkward.
Participants will attend a yoga class and stand in the front row. They will then write about their experience, and about how much they enjoyed the class.
Participants will be asked to tie their shoes, and then write a step-by-step explanation of how to tie their shoes. Their explanation's clarity will be measured.
Participants will look at advertisements in favor of smoking cigarettes. They will then be asked about their opinions on smoking.
Participants will interact with another person in the lab, and then rate how much they think the other person was sexually interested in him.
Participants will be instructed to throw darts at cutouts of past presidential candidates. Afterwards, they will be asked about their intention to vote in the next election.
Participants will be instructed to pick a pair of jeans from a closet that fit them. The jeans will all be labeled with sizes that are too small. Their self-esteem will be measured.
Participants who have never played a musical instrument will try to play a song on the piano. They will then rate how difficult the task was.
Participants will participate in a spelling bee in front of an audience, while being recorded on videotape. Their performance will be measured.
Participants will be given a riddle to solve and offered bad advice about solving it. How long it takes them to solve the problem will be recorded.
Participants will be asked to take a physics test. During the test, the experimenter will flirt with the participant. The participant's test performance will be measured.
Participants will take a spelling test, and then be accused of cheating. They will be told that they face legal action unless they confess. Their stress will be measured.
Participants at a table of food will be told to eat as much as they want. Sad music will play while they eat. Their food consumption rate will be recorded.
Participants will complete a puzzle on a table in a crowded coffee shop. The time it takes them to finish will be recorded.
Participants will be asked to memorize a passage under the influence of marijuana. Later, they will asked to recall the passage.
Participants will watch a series of commercials for diet pills, and then answer a survey designed to diagnose eating disorders.
Participants will engage in anonymous online chats with several other participants. They will then interact with each other in person. Their ability to guess who was who will be measured.

Participants will be asked to leave all of their belongings in a closet before completing a task. Upon their return they will be informed that their belongings were stolen. Their stress response will be recorded.
Participants will hear a recording of a telephone conversation, and then asked to write how they predict the conversation ended.
Participants will be asked to recall a traumatic experience from their life and write about it. They will be asked to rate their mood before and after this task.
Participants will come up with new flavors for ice cream. The originality of their flavors will be measured.
Participants will fill out an essay. While they work, a glass of water will be spilled on the essay and their pants. Their response will be recorded.
Participants who are smokers will be presented with negative and positive commercials about cigarette smoking. They will be asked to rate their quality and accuracy.
Participants will be asked to alphabetize a collection of books with unusual titles. Afterwards, they will be tested to see how many book titles they can remember.
Participants will read a paragraph of text and find all of the grammatical errors. Their accuracy will be measured.
Participants will have to answer a series of difficult questions from memory about their family's medical history. Afterwards, their distress will be measured.
Participants will be instructed to complete a high-intensity workout on a treadmill. They will then rate their self-esteem.
Participants will be left alone in a room with a wallet full of money. The experimenter will observe if the participant takes any of the contents of the wallet.
Participants will be shown violent and neutral photographs and asked to rate how they feel. Their heart rate will be measured.
Participants will be given a original painting and told to draw graffiti on it with a marker. Their willingness to do so will be recorded.
Participants will be asked to list songs that they find pleasant. They will then write an explanation of what they find pleasing in music. Their explanation will be analyzed.
Participants will run several laps around a track, but afterwards will only be offered hot coffee, not water. The amount they drink will be measured.
Participants will complete a series of strenuous cardiovascular exercises. They will then rate how they are feeling emotionally after the exercise.
Participants will be told they have won a large cash prize. Later they will be told the prize is not real, and their anger will be measured.
Participants will be asked to throw a frisbee as far as they can, and told that their ability will be posted on a public website. Their performance will be recorded.
Participants will be asked to walk around a building in very uncomfortable sneakers. They will then be asked to rate their mood.
Participants will leave their coats in a lab closet, and later be told that another person took their coat by mistake. Their emotional response will be measured.
Participants will fill out a personality test. They will be falsely told that they have an antisocial personality. Afterwards, their attitudes towards their friends will be measured.
Participants will look at an aerial photograph of a parking lot and identify all of the blue cars. Afterwards, they will take an eye test.
Participants who are dieting will be asked what food item they find the most difficult to resist. They will then see a series of images of this food, and their eye movements will be measured.
Participants will be asked to walk to a building within a time limit, but the room will be too far away to reach within that time. Their stress will be measured.
Participants will have to balance tennis balls on a dinner plate while standing on one foot. Afterwards, they will be asked questions about the experience.
Participants will be asked to assemble a Lego set while blindfolded. Their time and accuracy will be recorded.
Participants will engage in a text-based chat online. After, they will be asked to determine whether they are talking to a person or a robot. Their accuracy will be recorded.
Participants who have never had sex will have to fill out a survey about their knowledge of safe sex practices. Their embarrassment will be measured.
Participants will be told that there is a dangerous gas leak in the building. The amount of time that it takes them to safely leave the building will be timed.
Participants will be tickled by the experimenter until they feel uncomfortable or can't physically take it anymore. The amount of time they wait to disengage will be measured.
Participants will answer a survey designed to see if they have any symptoms of depression. They will also provide detailed information about any history of depression in their families.
Participants will watch a video of a cat being petted. They will then write an essay about their emotional state.
Participants will watch a video of animals being abused, and then will be asked to donate to an animal abuse prevention organization. Donation amounts will be recorded.
Participants will imagine how they would steal money from another person. Their anxiety about theft of their own belongings will then be measured.
Participants will hug a series of stuffed animal toys depicting various insects. They will then rate their mood and disgust level.
Participants will be asked to open a lock with a set of keys. However, none of the keys will work. The amount of time they keep trying will be recorded.
Participants will be left alone in a room without a clock or anything to do. Afterwards, they will be asked to guess how much time has passed.
Participants will have to write about a time that a family member made them feel bad during childhood. They will then rate their feelings towards that family member.
Participants will be instructed to take a brief nap. They will then complete a math test. Their test performance will be measured.
Participants who have anxiety disorders will be instructed to perform a series of meditation exercise, and then to rate their levels of anxiety.
Participants will be told that they are writing letters to a pen pal in another country. In reality, the letters are being thrown away. Their mood will be measured.
Participants will try on several pairs of pants in front of a distorted mirror that makes them look larger than they actually are. Their self esteem will be measured.
Participants will be given an adrenaline pill, but told that it is a sugar pill. They will then take a difficult math quiz. Their performance will be measured.
Participants will be asked to sit in a empty room without using their phones. A hidden camera will record whether or not they comply.
Participants will be told to solve a puzzle while remembering a series of 5-digit numbers. Their level of success will be recorded.
Participants will choose a glass of milk to drink while blindfolded. One glass will be rotten. They will be asked to write about their experience.
Participants will look at a set of photos of cats, and will rank them in order from most to least cute.
Participants will take a vocabulary test while eating cake. Their test performance and the amount they eat will be measured.
Participants will have to pour water from one glass into a series of smaller glasses, without spilling any. Their anxiety levels will be recorded.
Participants will be given a pill that makes them hyper-alert. They will then be scared by a person dressed in a monster mask. Their heart rate will be recorded.
Participants will be given a malfunctioning printer and asked to attempt to fix it. The time it takes for them to complete the task will be measured.
Participants will be instructed to punch a stuffed animal repeatedly. Their views on public funding for zoos will then be measured.
Participants from racial minorities will read a series of negative stereotypes about their race. They will then have to complete a timed math test. Their performance will be measured.
Participants will perform a variety of superstitious rituals before making a bet on a sports game. Afterwards, they will be asked about their odds of success in the bet.
Participants who are dieting will be given snacks with inaccurately low calorie counts. The calories consumed will be measured.
Participants will play a card game that requires them to keep track of which cards they've seen. Their memory for the cards will be measured.
Participants will be asked to take a nap. Shortly afterwards, an alarm clock will start beeping, and won't turn off until unplugged. The time taken to unplug will be measured.
Participants will complete a survey while hearing sexual noises from another room. At the end of the experience, participants will recall what they heard.
Participants will take part in a fake audition for a reality TV show in front of a panel of judges. Their speaking rate will be measured.
Participants will be randomly selected to play the role of either a prisoner or prison guard in a fake prison wing. Their behavior will be monitored.
Participants who smoke will be instructed to light a cigarette, but not to smoke it. They will then be asked to perform a reading task. Their performance will be measured.
Participants will be asked to identify famous landmarks from photos. Their accuracy will be recorded.
Participants will list as many United States presidents as they can remember. Afterwards, they will rate their interest in working for a government agency.
Participants will be asked to clip their nails while being recorded on video. They will then take a survey about the importance of personal hygiene.
Participants will be asked to complete a series of math tasks while memorizing an audio passage. Their math performance will be measured.
Participants will jog on a treadmill while happy and angry songs alternate on their headphones. Their jogging speed will be measured.
Participants will toss rubber balls into a small box from across a room. Their accuracy and enjoyment will be measured.
Participants will listen to a popular song and then be asked to sing the lyrics back. Their quality of singing will be measured.
Participants will be asked to read a newspaper in a dark room without a light. Their memory for the articles will be measured.
Participants will be instructed to order coffee at a diner and ask for free refills until they are refused. They will later write about their experience.
Participants will stick their hands into a bag and guess what they are touching. Inside will be dead bugs. Afterwards, they will rate how disgusted they were.
Participants will hear a series of notes played on the piano and will be asked to sing them back exactly as they were played. Their pitch will be recorded.
Participants will be asked to take a realistic baby doll and smash its head against a wall. Their willingness to do so and heart rate will be measured.
Participants who are male will complete a foot race in high heels. Their distance traveled before they stop will be recorded.
Participants will be asked to hold their breath while completing math tasks. Their completion time and number of correct answers will be recorded.
Participants will be asked to play a series of rigged gambling games where they will have one win after two losses. Their enjoyment of the games will be measured.
Participants will shoot at a target with a crossbow while listening to audio clips of murder victims screaming. Their accuracy will be recorded.
Participants will be given a caffeine dose without their knowledge, and asked to provide opinions on political issues and the environment.
Participants will make a list of the cities they would most like to visit around the world, and write about what they would do in each one.
Participants will rate their willingness to donate a money to different charities. The amount they offer to donate will be measured.
Participants will drink a large glass of water. Then will then have to complete a long series of math problems before they are allowed to go to the bathroom.
Participants will be shown images of famous pornographic actors and actresses and asked if they recognize them. Their hesitation before answering will be recorded.
Participants will have to count backwards from 1000 in front of an audience, and then give a public speech about their personal weaknesses. Their anxiety level will be measured.
Participants will create a fake online dating profile with the goal of getting as many date requests as possible. Their vocabulary choice will be recorded.
Participants will participate in a practice interview for a corporate position. They will then be told that they did very well. Their reaction will be observed.
Participants who normally wear glasses will be asked to perform small manual tasks without their glasses. Their performance on the tasks will be measured.
Participants will listen to classical music and be asked to identify the tempo and rhythmic signatures of the pieces they hear. Their accuracy will be measured.
Participants will try to catch as many flies as they can using only their hands. The number of flies they catch will be recorded..
Participants will be asked to view images of heterosexual and homosexual couples kissing. They will have to pair each image with positive or negative words.
Participants will be instructed to make up a dance and perform it in a public space. Their anxiety will be measured.
Participants will be asked to complete a number of memory and mathematical tasks while listening to fast-paced and loud music.
Participants will be asked to complete a survey about their knowledge about government spending. Their political views will be recorded.
Participants will be blindfolded and led into a room of garbage that has been sprayed with perfume. The amount of time they stay in the room will be measured.
Participants will view a series of flowers, and then take a survey that measures personality traits related to creativity and openness to change.
Participants will be asked to list their five favorite friends from grade school. They will then indicate if they still keep in touch with any of them.
Participants will use marijuana in the lab. They will then be given a selection of snacks, while the experimenter keeps track of how much they eat.
Participants will be asked to sit outside in the sun on a hot day, until they get a sunburn. They will then try several flavors of ice cream and rate how much they liked each one.
Participants will be scared by a loud noise and then asked to watch threatening videos. Afterwards, their sensitivity to loud noises will be measured.
Participants will read articles about several office cultures, and will be asked to predict how effective the office environments are for employee productivity.
Participants from racial minorities will read negative stereotypes about their racial group. Their self-esteem will be measured.
Participants will spend time interacting with several dogs. Afterwards, they will rate how happy or sad they usually feel, as well as their current mood.
Participants will play a game that requires them to remember a pattern of colored lights while answering simple math problems. Their performance in the game will be measured.
Participants will be asked to impersonate a celebrity and take a personality test pretending to be the celebrity. Their responses will be recorded.
Participants will play a game of catch with two other people, who will never throw the ball to them. Their feelings of social isolation will be measured.
Participants will hold their eyes open for as long as they can without blinking. Every time they blink, a loud buzzer will sound. Their mood will be measured.
Participants will sample different spicy foods without water. They will then be asked to rate the spiciness of each dish on a numerical scale.
Participants will be given candies to eat that are unexpectedly spicy. They will then fill out a questionnaire about what they experienced.
Participants will sample different ice cream flavors and rate how each flavor makes them feel on a scale from 1 to 5.
Participants will receive a wrapped present after answering a demographics survey. The box will contain dead spiders. Their reaction will be observed.
Participants will be asked to draw the layout of keys on a keyboard from memory. Their accuracy will be measured.
Participants will read a series of essays in favor of lowering taxes. They will then be asked about their opinions on tax policy.
Participants will be given a coloring book and asked to color in as many pictures as possible before time runs out. The number of pictures will be counted.

Participants who have never driven a manual transmission car will be asked to drive on the highway for several miles without being told that the car is manual. Their adrenaline levels will be measured.
Participants will be asked to eat raw cookie dough after watching a video about childhood obesity. The amount of cookie dough they eat will be measured.
Participants will be asked to swallow a spoonful of ground cinnamon. This will make them vomit. Afterwards , they will report their attitude towards several foods that contain cinnamon.
Participants will eat cookies and rate how they feel after each one. They will be given more and more cookies until they refuse to continue.
Participants will complete a difficult math test. During it, a loud alarm will be audible in the background. Their frustration levels and test performance will be observed.
Participants will have to keep their hands in a pot of water until a bell rings. The water will slowly become very hot. Their endurance time will be recorded.
Participants will see a series of shapes and have to identify how many sides and corners each shape has. Their accuracy will be recorded.
Participants will be asked how skilled they are as drivers compared to the average person. They will then have to complete a drivers test. Their performance will be measured.
Participants will have several alcoholic beverages and then view a series of online dating profiles. They will rate attractiveness of each profile subject. Their ratings will be recorded.
Participants will be asked to calculate appropriate tips for a series of restaurant bills of different amounts, without using a calculator.
Participants will eat ice cream in a room with air conditioning. The amount of ice cream consumed will be recorded.
Participants will review resumes and photos for potential job candidates. They will then have to select candidates to hire based only on their physical appearance.
Participants will eat chocolate bars shaped like male and female genitals. Their arousal level and appetite will be measured.
Participants will be asked to stand in a walk-in freezer for as long as they can. Their level of confidence will be recorded.
Participants' faces will be recorded while they smell ammonia, look at unpleasant photos, and touch frogs. Their expressions will be measured and analyzed.
Participants will be instructed to play a video game, and will then sort paperwork. Their level of boredom will be measured.
Participants will be instructed to pull a fire alarm in a crowded building. Their willingness to comply will be observed.
Participants will be asked to speak with a toddler for one hour. Their vocabulary usage will be recorded.
Participants will donate blood, and then told falsely that their donated blood will be sent to prison hospitals to treat convicted sex offenders. Their distress will be measured.
Participants will begin an online survey until the computer shuts down unexpectedly. The amount of time passed until they seek help will be measured.
Participants will play ping pong against a professional, and their score will be publicly ranked compared to every previous participant in the study. Their embarrassment will be measured.
Participants will be asked to brush their teeth and then drink an entire can of soda. They will then give their opinions on dental hygiene.
Participants who have recently experienced a breakup will be asked to sit in a room, listen to a sad song, and try not to cry. Their facial expressions will be recorded.
Participants will answer geography questions, and will be falsely told that all of their answers are incorrect. Afterwards they will be asked how confident they were in their answers.
Participants will be given a generic painkiller and then asked to write about a time that they were made to feel socially excluded. The vividness of their memory will be recorded.
Participants will have their heart rate and blood pressure measured while completing a survey about their self esteem and confidence.
Participants will be given painkillers and then asked to write about an embarrassing social experience. Their amount of embarrassment will be measured.
NOT FOUND
Participants will be given an injection that temporarily paralyzes facial muscles. Their emotional responses to  photographs will then be measured.
Participants will list all the foods they ate in the past week. They will then take a survey about their level of satisfaction with their current diet and body image.
Participants will watch a video of a dinner party where a guest apologizes for a rude joke. They will indicate whether the apology made the party more or less awkward.
Participants will put their hand in a very cold bucket of water, and keep it there for as long as they can endure.
Participants will view images of racially ambiguous individuals and will be asked to guess what race each person is.
Participants will watch a video of a speech with no sound. They will then be asked to judge the quality of speech.
Participants will read short biographical summaries of different politicians, and will be asked to make predictions about their personality traits.
Participants will take a personality survey, and then list the number of cities in which they've lived. The distance between the cities will be measured.
Participants will write a story about their significant other cheating on them. They will then be asked to call their significant other, and vocal stress patterns will be analyzed.
Participants who are sleep-deprived will complete a math test in the lab. Their scores and eyesight ability will be recorded.
Participants will give a public speech while wearing very itchy underwear. Their speaking ability will be rated.
Participants will be given a marshmallow and told that they can eat it right away, or wait five minutes to receive two marshmallows. Their ability to wait will be recorded.
Participants will be asked to taste different brands of chocolate and read about how much they cost. They will then rate how much they like each brand.
Participants will think about the worst present they've gotten for a holiday. They will then answer questions about their self-esteem.
Participants will answer questions about the features that they think are the most and least important when buying a car.
Participants will draw a picture representing their biggest fears. They will then rate how scary the drawing and their fears seem.
Participants will have their photograph taken, and will receive fake feedback about their attractiveness. They will then be asked about their levels of self-esteem.
Participants will be weighed, and will then be asked to look at fashion magazines featuring underweight models. They will be asked to fill out a self-esteem survey.
Participants will describe the clothes they wear most often in the workplace, and will be told that it is unprofessional. Their willingness to buy new clothes will be measured.
Participants will be asked to rate attractiveness of people in group photos, both together as a group and then individually.
Participants will be left alone in a room with a baby and told they have to take care of it during the study. Their nervousness and the baby's distress will be measured.
Participants will sign up to receive information about their family history. They will falsely be told that an ancestor was a serial killer. Their feelings will be measured.
Participants will rapidly view a series of pictures of men and women, and will predict each person's sexual orientation. Accuracy will be measured.
Participants will be instructed to drive a car into a wall at a low speed. The speed they drive during the crash will be measured.
Participants will write an essay about what it would be like to be in solitary confinement in a prison. Their support for solitary confinement will then be measured.
Participants will play a poker with another person who is wearing very visible underwear. The participant's ability to bluff successfully will be measured.
Participants will draw a family tree with as many family members as they can remember. They will then indicate how difficult it was to recall each family member.
Participants will be shown videos of serious car accidents, and then asked to use a driving simulator machine. Their caution while driving will be measured.
Participants will watch a video about folding origami animals, and will then practice origami themselves. Afterwards, they will rate how difficult it was.
Participants who identify as homosexual will be asked to view photos of members of the opposite sex and will be asked to identify their attractive features.
Participants will receive a call on their cell phone from a wrong number. The number will call more five times. The participant's politeness in responding will be measured.
Participants will list their favorite songs and movies from ten years earlier. They will then answer questions about how energetic they feel.
Participants will teach a puppy to sit in exchange for a treat. The time and treats needed to teach the puppy will be measured.
Participants will be asked to read a series of jokes and rate how funny each one is, on a scale from 1 to 100.
Participants will be asked to taste different sodas while blindfolded and determine which flavors are which. Their accuracy will be measured.
Participants taking a survey will hear cries coming from another room. The cries will continue until they go to help or finish the survey. Their behavior will be observed.
Participants will be told that they qualify for a large scholarship. They will be told that the scholarship is not real, and their disappointment will be measured.
Participants will have to walk around a city block with a very heavy backpack. Afterwards, they will be asked questions about the people they saw during their walk.
Participants will either listen to a song played on a guitar. Afterwards they will decide whether the song was live or recorded, and indicate their confidence in their decision.
Participants' heart rates will be measured while they write short essays about three personal life events, ranging from mildly to extremely stressful.
Participants who are on a diet will be asked to choose unhealthy foods to eat for dinner. Their choices will be recorded.
Participants will provide their home addresses, and will be signed up for junkmail subscriptions without their permission. Their frustration will be measured.
Participants will participate in a speed dating activity. They will be told that no one was interested in seeing them again. Their mood will be measured.
Participants will be shown blurry photographs and will be asked to identify what each photograph depicts. Their accuracy will be measured.
Participants will watch a video of a cat being killed. They will then write an essay about their emotional state.
Participants will be given alcohol to drink until they are intoxicated. They will then perform a memory task while intoxicated, and again when sober.
Participants who stutter will undergo a speech therapy session, where they receive positive encouragement. Afterwards, their level of stuttering will be measured.
Participants will view photographs of dead human bodies, and attempt to guess how each person died. Their accuracy will be measured.
Participants will smell a variety of flowers and rank them in the order of their most to least favorite. Their mood will be measured.
Participants will sit in a fitness class at a gym that is far beyond their level of physical ability. Their motivation to exercise in the future will be measured.
Participants will reflect on the most embarrassing moment of their childhood for five minutes, and then write an essay on confidence. The essay length will be measured.
Participants will asked to give detailed lists of their past sexual partners and activities, ranked from best to worst. The length of their lists and age will be recorded.
Participants will play a game where their age is guessed by the experimenter. The experimenter will purposefully guess an age ten years too old. Their self-esteem will be measured.
Participants will drink orange juice and then complete an ice-cream taste test. The amount of ice cream they consume will be recorded.
Participants will be asked to think about their favorite meal from childhood. They will be asked to rate how satisfied and hungry they feel on 1-10 scales.
Participants will be given a large bucket of marbles. They will be timed as they to move all of the marbles into another bucket, one at a time.
Participants will be asked to let a professional boxer punch them in the stomach. The boxer will pretend to punch, and whether or not the participant flinches will be recorded.
Participants will be given a taste test, and then falsely told that one of the drinks they sampled was contaminated with fecal bacteria. Their heart rate will be observed.
Participants will be asked their attitudes about a celebrity before and after reading short excerpts of their autobiography. The change in their attitudes will be measured.
Participants will be given a box by a stranger, and told to hide it from the police. Whether or not they instead contact the police will be recorded.
Participants will listen to various loud and quiet sounds with headphones. While they listen, their eye blink rate will be measured.
Participants will be asked to eat a very spicy pepper without anything to drink. Their anxiety levels will be measured.
Participants will complete a long survey, and be told that it took twice as long as it actually did. They will then report their level of boredom.
Participants will be asked to remember as many of their Facebook friends as possible. Afterwards, they will answer questions about how many friends they have relative to other people.
Participants will be asked to do yoga exercises. Afterwards, they will answer questions about their level of relaxation and quality of life.
Participants will be shown a series of online dating profiles. They will decide if they would go on a date with the people from each profile.
Participants will be eat a series of different cupcakes, and come up with creative names for each one to be used in a cupcake store menu. Their mood will be measured.
Participants will read about a series of legal disputes, and asked to determine who is at fault in each case.
Participants will view images of cars. They will have to write down how much they like each car on a scale from 1 to 10.
Participants will be asked to list every place where they spent money in the past week. They will then provide income information and predictions about future income.
Participants will be asked to view pictures of real faces and computer-generated faces side-by-side. They will rate which faces are more attractive.
Participants will see a series of faces and attempt to classify their gender as quickly as possible. Their accuracy will be measured.
Participants will be asked to engage in an online chat with a stranger and rate their interaction in a variety of ways.
Participants will read a series of positive news article about their hometown. Their opinions about their hometown will then be measured.
Participants will be asked to fill out a long and difficult survey, and then to do it all again when the original copy is thrown away. Their levels of frustration will be observed.
Participants will be offered two cups of coffee and then asked to memorize a poem. Their memory and mood will be measured.
Participants entering the lab will see an old woman pretending to have difficulty carrying a package. The amount of help they offer will be recorded.
Participants will be asked to answer reading comprehension questions from a standardized test meant for third-graders. Performances will be measured.
NOT FOUND
Participants will be blindfolded, spun around several times, and asked to pick up toothpicks off of a table. The number of toothpicks they can pick up will be recorded.
Participants will read an article written to make them feel very proud, and will then be asked to estimate their own height.
Participants will be blindfolded and given a box of chocolates. They will be asked to guess the flavor of each chocolate.
Participants will be given a sugar pill and take a survey. The temperature of the room will slowly rise, and participant distress will be recorded.
Participants will be asked to solve a jigsaw puzzle, and then to take photographs to put on a future puzzle. The content of the photographs will be recorded.
Participants will be asked to create a structure with toy blocks that represents their personality. The shape they build will be analyzed.
Participants will be asked to read a series of news articles and rate how trustworthy they seem.
Participants will get to sample different flavors of juice while having their brain activity measured. The amount of juice they consume will be measured.
Participants will be asked to eat various kind of salad. Their chewing speed will be recorded.
Participants will look at a book about famous paintings. They will rate how beautiful they think each painting is on a scale from 1 to 10.
Participants will be told that they will be meeting another person and having a conversation. They will then rate their level of interest in the meeting.
Participants will watch videos of people reading statements about themselves. They will have to indicate if each statement is true or a lie. Accuracy will be measured.
Participants will be asked to study a math textbook in either a room with brightly colored walls. They will then be quizzed on the material they studied.
Participants will eat a protein bar and asked to take a vocabulary test. Performance and blood sugar levels will be measured.
Participants will watch videos of people helping strangers in public. They will then rate how kind each act is.
Participants will sharpen a box of pencils, and then use them to write an essay about the value of hard work. Their persuasiveness will be rated.
